metadata.intro: The quantum mechanical program replaces the deterministic trajectories of classical physics with the probabilistic evolution of state vectors within an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. From the historical resolution of the ultraviolet catastrophe to the rigorous axiomatic formulation of the measurement postulate, this roadmap navigates the non-local correlations, operator algebras, and wave-particle dualities that define the subatomic regime.

bridges.classical-mechanics: The correspondence principle ensures that quantum expectation values follow Newtonian trajectories in the macroscopic limit, as formalized by Ehrenfest's Theorem.
bridges.relativity: The unification of quantum mechanics and special relativity necessitates a covariant field-theoretic approach, leading to the Dirac equation and the prediction of antimatter.
bridges.theoretical-physics: The mathematical foundations of quantum theory, including spectral theory and group representation, provide the primary toolkit for modern gauge theories and the Standard Model.

pillars.title: 1. The Ultraviolet Resolution
pillars.narrative: The historical transition from classical continuity to discrete energy levels, established through the resolution of the photoelectric effect and blackbody radiation.

pillars.title: 2. The Matter-Wave Manifold
pillars.narrative: Defining the 4D phase relationship between momentum and wavelength, establishing the wave-packet as the primary ontological unit of the subatomic regime.

pillars.title: 3. Hilbert Space Formalism
pillars.narrative: Constructing the rigorous inner product space required to maintain the statistical integrity of the wave function within a square-integrable manifold.

pillars.title: 4. Axiomatic Measurement & Statistics
pillars.narrative: Codifying the measurement postulate and the collapse of the state vector as the transition from unitary evolution to thermodynamic classicality.

pillars.title: 5. Quantized Potentials & Dynamics
pillars.narrative: Exploring the discrete eigenspectra generated by boundary conditions and the non-classical leakage of state vectors through potential barriers.

pillars.title: 6. Wave-Particle Duality, Complementarity & Path Integrals
pillars.narrative: Connecting the Born probability interpretation, unitary probability conservation, Bohr complementarity, and Feynman's sum-over-histories formulation.

pillars.title: 7. Atomic Physics, Spin & Quantum Scattering
pillars.narrative: Intrinsic spin quantization, external electromagnetic level splittings, relativistic atomic structure, scattering amplitudes, and non-classical bosonic field states.

pillars.title: 8. Open Quantum Systems, Quantum Optics & Quantum Information
pillars.narrative: Dissipative quantum dynamics, strong light-matter coupling in optical resonators, unitary quantum logic, fault-tolerant error correction, and non-classical photon statistics.

pillars.title: 9. Molecular Physics & Ultracold AMO
pillars.narrative: Born-Oppenheimer molecular orbitals and potential surfaces, rovibrational and Raman spectroscopy, Doppler laser cooling and optical tweezers, Paul/Penning ion traps and optical atomic clocks, and Rydberg-atom quantum simulators.

pillars.title: 10. Quantum Approximation & Many-Body Methods
pillars.narrative: Semiclassical WKB tunneling and Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization, time-dependent perturbation theory and Fermi's golden rule, angular momentum coupling via the Wigner-Eckart theorem, self-consistent Hartree-Fock and density functional theory, and identical particles with second quantization in Fock space.
